chapter: Stuff Smith Trio and New York
title: Joining the Stuff Smith Trio and being talked into New York
summary: John Levy writes to Jones, then working outside Chicago with Johnnie Board, to join Stuff Smith's violin-piano-bass trio and move to New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: At the end of the other tape you were just starting to mention something about the Stuff Smith Trio.

Yes. That was a great experience. In fact it really triggered me off and triggered John Levy off in New York, because at the time in Chicago we'd made a pretty nice reputation, and we were getting good reviews and so consequently when we got to New York, everybody on opening night was in the house. But I was the one that didn't want to go. I was young and I was in love with a little girl around Chicago. I didn't think I wanted to go to New York at that point, you know. So John Levy told me, says, "Well, let's go, and --," the contract was for 10 weeks with a 10 week option. And he said, "Well, take it as a vacation," you know? Oh, he conned me into it.

Yes. And when we got -- the first day I set foot in New York I knew I wasn't ever going to live in Chicago again. I fell in love with the city, you know? And, oh, we did quite well there, you know. It was a very unique trio. Violin, piano and bass, playing jazz.
How did you happen to get together in the first place?
Well, Stuff and John were working together in Chicago, and there was another fine piano player,

fine pianist, Raymond Walters, was playing piano. And I think Raymond left the trio for one reason or the other. And John wrote me a letter. I was just working with a small group, a local group, just around outside of Chicago.
Oh, let me see. Des Moines, Cedar Rapids, Springfield, Illinois. Those kinds of towns, you know?

Oh, a guy named Johnnie Board. He's a fine musician but he's still there. Earl Phillips is another, a good drummer. Gee, I can't think of -- that goes back a good while now. It's hard for me to remember those names, you know?
Who was the leader of the group?
